sources.text:
The Kornati archipelago (pronounced [kɔ̝rnǎːti]) of Croatia, also known as the Stomorski islands, is located in the northern part of Dalmatia, south from Zadar and west from Šibenik, in the Šibenik-Knin County. With 35 kilometres (22 miles) length and 89 islands, some large, some small, in a sea area of about 320 square kilometres (124 sq mi), the Kornati are the densest archipelago in the Mediterranean Sea. From northwest to southeast (from the island of Balabra to Samograd), and from northeast to southwest (from Gangarol to Mana) they stretch for 13 km (8 miles). The name of the archipelago is the plural form of the name of the largest island, called Kornat.


== Settlement ==
There are no permanent settlements in Kornati. Simple houses in well-protected coves such as Vrulje, Kravjačica, Lavsa and others are used by mainland landowners as temporary shelters. Most of the land owners are from the island of Murter and Dugi Otok.


== Climate ==
The average monthly temperature for January is 7.3 °C (45.1 °F), in July it is 23.9 °C (75.0 °F); the average sea temperature in winter is 14 to 15 °C (57 to 59 °F) and in summer 22.8 °C (73.0 °F).

stops.name: Kornati
stops.detail: Das Kornati-Archipel Kroatiens, auch bekannt als die Stomorski-Inseln, liegt im nördlichen Teil Dalmatiens, südlich von Zadar und westlich von Šibenik, im Kreis Šibenik-Knin. Mit 35 Kilometern Länge und 89 Inseln, teils groß, teils klein, in einem Meeresgebiet von etwa 320 Quadratkilometern sind die Kornati das dichteste Archipel im Mittelmeer. Von Nordwesten nach Südosten und von Nordosten nach Südwesten erstrecken sie sich über 13 km. Der Name des Archipels ist die Pluralform des Namens der größten Insel, genannt Kornat.
